text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 continues to circulate in Europe, even though the World Health Organization declared it no longer a public health emergency of international concern in May 2023. While the most severe cases can still lead to serious complications, most people experience mild to moderate symptoms and recover without specific treatment, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control.
Key points about COVID-19 in Europe:

list.title: Ongoing Circulation:
list.snippet: The virus is still present in communities, and it's important to be aware of the risks.

list.title: Vulnerable Groups:
list.snippet: Individuals over 60, pregnant women, and people with underlying health conditions are more susceptible to severe illness.

list.title: Varying Symptoms:
list.snippet: COVID-19 symptoms can range from asymptomatic to severe respiratory issues.

list.title: Public Health Response:
list.snippet: Organizations like the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) have played a crucial role in disease surveillance and supporting countries during the pandemic.

list.title: Continued Monitoring:
list.snippet: While the emergency phase is over, the virus is still being monitored, and public health measures may be adjusted as needed.
